Pass with caveats. The paper cites the clinical ACE-Q (Murphy, Steele, Steele, Allman, Kastner & Dube, 2016), a paywalled book chapter, whose exact phrasing could not be obtained, so a wording variant relative to the standard handout is possible. Item identity is not in doubt -- the codes name their own ACE category.

(2) cov_group is transposed relative to the source paper. The 21-record S1 file (IRW cov_group=patient, 20 ids with ACE data) reproduces the paper's CAREGIVER endorsement counts exactly for 9/10 categories with denominator 21 (swear 8/38.1%, push 5/23.8%, touch 0, loved 5/23.8%, eat 0, divorced 6/28.6%, mother 2/9.5%, drugs 9/42.9%, depressed 5/23.8%), and its BAI total mean is 8.4 vs 19.9 in the 37-record S2 file, matching the paper's finding that patients are more anxious than caregivers. Affects all five esiason_2024_* tables, not just this one; does not affect item text.

(3) One source-vs-paper discrepancy inside that subset: the paper reports 2 caregivers endorsing 'household member imprisoned' (9.5%), while the deposited file records 0 for the prison item. The other nine counts match exactly. Recorded, not reconciled.
(4) The S2 file holds 37 complete records while the paper reports 31 patients recruited and computes patient ACE percentages over n=30. Not investigated further; outside item-text scope.

BLOCKED on rights, no CSV written. The instrument is the Valued Living Questionnaire Part 2 (consistency ratings, Wilson & Groom 2002). The Esiason 2024 PLOS ONE deposit (CC BY 4.0) publishes NO VLQ wording -- the S1/S2 REDCap XLSX exports carry only the bare column codes fam2..phsy2 with no label row and no value labels, and no table, figure or appendix reproduces the items -- so the wording could only come from the VLQ form itself, whose footer states on both pages: "Copyright © 2002, by Kelly Wilson. You may reproduce and use this form at will for the purpose of treatment and research. You may not distribute it without the express written consent of the author." -- footer printed on BOTH pages of the VLQ form (Wilson & Groom 2002, revised 4 October 2006; contact kwilson@olemiss.edu). Shipping item text is distributing that wording to third parties, which fires itemtext_standard.md's 2026-09-04 no-redistribution ruling (DSES/Fetzer), a ruling that explicitly overrides the openly licensed source deposit. RETRY TEST: "Would an unchanged retry, right now, plausibly produce a different result?" -- NO. This is a determinate verdict (licence bars reuse); the source was located, read and quoted, and no access failure occurred. What would flip it: express written consent from Kelly Wilson (kwilson@olemiss.edu), or a ruling by Ben that a "may not distribute" clause on a freely reproducible clinical form does not fire the no-redistribution rule. ESCALATION: the same clause covers esiason_2024_vlq_importance (Part 1 of the identical form, another agent's table in this same batch) and every other VLQ table in the queue -- this is a class decision, not a per-table one. MAPPING, recorded so an unblock needs no rework: verify_esiason_2024_vlq_consistency.R passes -- item codes are self-describing domain mnemonics that ARE the source column names, marr2 (n=53) and par2 (n=49) are the two lowest-n items of ten (the rest 54-56) as the two non-universal VLQ domains must be, and each of the 10 consistency items correlates more strongly with its own importance twin than with the mean of the other nine (own r 0.123-0.587 vs mean-other 0.056-0.222).

Every source needed was retrieved successfully. To flip it, one of two things would have to change: express written consent from Kelly Wilson (kwilson@olemiss.edu) to distribute the form, or a ruling by Ben that the 2026-09-04 no-redistribution rule does not reach the VLQ.
